subject: Pilot: usage-floor vs. credit-rebate structure — runway & SLA questions
messages:
From: Kendra James <kendra@brightdata.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Sep 20, 2026 at 15:10 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing structure question — usage-floor vs rebate

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looks promising. We're planning a 30-day time-boxed evaluation of Redwood's hosted inference for a customer-facing feature and have a quick pricing / packaging question before we lock the SOW.

Primary concern: early-stage usage will be low while we finish integration, so a straight commit feels risky for BrightData. Two options our procurement team floated:
- a small usage-floor (minimum commit) with a rebate if actual usage falls below the floor; or
- a non-refundable credit bucket we draw from (no rebate) but at a deeper discount.

We'd like to:
1) Understand how Redwood would define the rebate trigger (e.g., percent of floor, time windows),
2) See any constraints on converting rebates to future credits rather than cash refunds, and
3) Confirm whether onboarding SLAs / dedicated onboarding time can be rolled into the pilot price (to speed integration).

Can you share a short SOW and a few illustrative numbers we can show procurement? Also — is there a one-week "runway buffer" option if we spike usage during load tests?

Appreciate a quick note — procurement deadline is next Friday.

Best,
Kendra
Kendra James
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightData AI
[Attachment: Usage_Baseline_Q3.csv (9 KB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kendra James <kendra@brightdata.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Sep 21, 2026 at 10:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing structure question — usage-floor vs rebate

Hi Kendra — thanks for the clear framing. I've attached a short draft SOW (POC_SOW_v2.pdf) and an outline of the two approaches below. Quick summary first, then a proposed set of guardrails.

Approach A — Usage-floor + rebate
- Customer commits to a minimum token/embedding floor for the 30-day window (example: $6k floor).
- If actual consumption < 60% of the floor across the 30-day window, Redwood issues a rebate equal to the unused portion *at the paid rate* or, per request, converts to future platform credits (no cash-out).
- Rebate calculation windows are aligned to the full pilot period (we don't prorate weekly unless agreed).

Approach B — Prepaid credit bucket (deeper discount)
- One-time credit purchase that covers the trial. No rebate.
- Unused credits can be rolled to a future invoice within 90 days if you convert to a committed plan.

Onboarding SLA / Runway buffer
- We can include a 2-day dedicated onboarding block (two engineer-days) included in the pilot price; if the integration completes earlier, the time is retained as engineering support credits.
- Runway buffer: we can provision a one-time 10% bonus credit pool for week 1 to absorb test spikes; if used, that consumption counts against the floor/bucket.

Tradeoffs (so procurement can decide):
- Usage-floor + rebate keeps vendor risk shared but requires measurement windows and a rebate mechanism (prefer convert-to-credits to avoid accounting churn).
- Credit bucket is simpler for procurement but gives less upside to the customer if they scale in the pilot.

I've proposed illustrative numbers in the attached SOW (two options side-by-side). If helpful I can route a concise note to finance/ops for an approval playbook.

Next steps: if you prefer rebate -> credits, I'll loop in our sales ops and legal to adjust the SOW and capture the exact rebate formula.

Onboarding: are you available for a 30-minute kickoff this Thursday?

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
+1 415 555 0198
[Attachment: POC_SOW_v2.pdf (15 KB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 22, 2026 at 09:15 -0700
Subject: FW: Pilot pricing structure question — usage-floor vs rebate

Marissa / Karthik — FYI, BrightData prefers either a usage-floor with a rebate or a prepaid credit bucket. Procurement wants the rebate math spelled out and is open to converting rebates to platform credits rather than cash refunds.

Proposed for approval (illustrative):
- Floor example: $6,000 for 30 days.
- Rebate trigger: if actual billed consumption <= 60% of floor, rebate equals the unused portion at the paid rate, converted to Redwood credits valid for 180 days.
- Onboarding concession: include 2 engineer-days (valued at $2,400) as part of pilot; if used, count as credit applied to the floor.
- Runway buffer: 10% bonus credits for week 1.
- Discount/concession ask: 15% net off list for the pilot (applied to the billable token rates); in the rebate scenario the rebate is computed on the discounted rate.

Questions for you two:
1) Legal implication of converting rebates to credits (Marissa — do we need explicit language or is a simple credit memo clause sufficient?),
2) Finance — is a 180-day credit expiration OK (Karthik?), and do we prefer credits vs invoice refund for accounting cleanliness?,
3) Should we present both options in the SOW or pick one to simplify procurement's decision?

I'm recommending we offer convert-to-credit only (no cash rebates) to keep the operational flow simple. Procurement tends to prefer credits if they plan to continue; cash refunds complicate recognition. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Irene

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Sep 23, 2026 at 14:45 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Pilot pricing structure question — usage-floor vs rebate

Irene — good framing. My position: convert-to-credits only, yes, but tweak the floor so procurement doesn't balk. Two pragmatic adjustments:

1) Reduce the suggested floor to $4,000 for a 30-day pilot (instead of $6k). That keeps us protected for basic infra while lowering procurement friction.
2) If usage <= 50% of the floor, convert the unused portion into credits valid for 1 year (gives customer more runway and reduces renewal objections).
3) Approve a 12% net concession off list for this pilot (sales-led concession band). Anything beyond that requires manager sign-off.

Legal note: include a short clause in the SOW that rebates will be issued as non-transferable platform credits; finance will not issue refunds. Karthik — can you confirm revenue recognition implications for 1-year credits? If that's a problem, we can reduce to 180 days.

Irene — please update the SOW, include a single-option recommendation (floor + convert-to-credit) and route for signature. Add a DocuSign flow and put procurement contact as procurement@brightdata.ai.

-Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
[Internal: approved concession 12%]

From: Kendra James <kendra@brightdata.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot pricing structure question — usage-floor vs rebate

Hi Irene / Marissa — thanks for the fast follow. Procurement is happy to proceed on the convert-to-credits path with the adjusted floor and one-year credit window. A few quick asks so we can finalize:

1) Please add a short definition in the SOW for "active inference call" (we propose: any successful generation request that returns at least one token and counts against the token pool).
2) Add a KPI baseline section referencing the attached Usage_Baseline_Q3.csv so both sides have an agreed starting point.
3) Please send the DocuSign SOW (we'll have procurement@brightdata.ai countersign).

If you can get the SOW in DocuSign by EOD Monday we'll route it on our side and aim to start integration the following week. Looking forward.

Best,
Kendra
